explanations.img_0eryguqq:
- ETD-dark solid is 5.706%, versus means of 2.495% for Batch_1, 2.956% for Batch_2 and 4.594% for Batch_3, so it is closest to Batch_3.
- Opposing: for Batch_3 versus Batch_1, the reported model-score contribution is -1.418 score from segmented pore area and -0.592 score from all-pore minus deep-pore area; both negative terms oppose Batch_3.
- ETD-dark solid (5.706%) is dark in ETD but solid in BSE. SE and BSE signals come from different depths, so this can reflect detector contrast. It does not by itself identify sub-surface pores, and beam conditions are unknown.
- A segmented pore area of 14.75% is a 2-D area share. Total porosity can include connected and unconnected pore volume, so this value alone does not establish connectivity, tortuosity or performance.
- Acquisition properties alone predict batch in training, so a match may reflect imaging session rather than material. The graphite-versus-binder split is experimental, and the sampling intervals overlap several batch ranges; overlap is not batch equivalence.

claims.text: ETD-dark solid is 5.706%, versus means of 2.495% for Batch_1, 2.956% for Batch_2 and 4.594% for Batch_3, so it is closest to Batch_3.

Opposing: for Batch_3 versus Batch_1, the reported model-score contribution is -1.418 score from segmented pore area and -0.592 score from all-pore minus deep-pore area; both negative terms oppose Batch_3.

ETD-dark solid (5.706%) is dark in ETD but solid in BSE. SE and BSE signals come from different depths, so this can reflect detector contrast. It does not by itself identify sub-surface pores, and beam conditions are unknown.

citations.quote: Secondary electrons (SE) are very low energy (<50eV) electrons, and as such escape from only near the surface of the sample.

claims.text: A segmented pore area of 14.75% is a 2-D area share. Total porosity can include connected and unconnected pore volume, so this value alone does not establish connectivity, tortuosity or performance.

citations.quote: In the normalized intrusion curve, this connected porosity region is also the ratio of connected pore volume to total pore volume or the percent of total porosity.

S7116122739bfe6d4965d.title: JEOL: low-kV SEM imaging and detector contrast
S7116122739bfe6d4965d.text:
All SEMs use two basic imaging detectors/signals for most applications. Secondary electrons (SE) are very low energy (<50eV) electrons, and as such escape from only near the surface of the sample. In general they are considered to carry only “topographic” surface information. These electrons are typically collected with an Everhart-Thornley scintillator/photomultiplier detector with a bias on it to attract the low energy electrons to the detector. Backscattered electrons (BSE) are higher energy electrons (up to nearly the accelerating voltage of the incident beam) and as such escape from a much deeper & wider volume of excitation within the sample. In general they are considered to carry only “Z contrast” (contrast based on differences in mean atomic number or average density). These electrons are typically collected with a solid state or YAG detector placed directly above the sample. Because the BSEs are high energy there is no collection bias on this detector and the detected electrons are “line of sight.”

While both of the previous definitions are true they do not paint a complete picture. One of the most common questions asked about any SEM is “What is the resolution?” This is a question with seemingly many different answers and most of them seem non-intuitive! One has to first define what type of electrons you are measuring with (SE or BSE), and what are the SEM operating parameters such as: kV, WD and probe current (often loosely defined as spot size or probe diameter).

Resolution and Contrast Mechanisms

## img_0eryguqq: Batch_3

- ETD-dark solid is 5.706%, versus means of 2.495% for Batch_1, 2.956% for Batch_2 and 4.594% for Batch_3, so it is closest to Batch_3.
- Opposing: for Batch_3 versus Batch_1, the reported model-score contribution is -1.418 score from segmented pore area and -0.592 score from all-pore minus deep-pore area; both negative terms oppose Batch_3.
- ETD-dark solid (5.706%) is dark in ETD but solid in BSE. SE and BSE signals come from different depths, so this can reflect detector contrast. It does not by itself identify sub-surface pores, and beam conditions are unknown.
- A segmented pore area of 14.75% is a 2-D area share. Total porosity can include connected and unconnected pore volume, so this value alone does not establish connectivity, tortuosity or performance.
- Acquisition properties alone predict batch in training, so a match may reflect imaging session rather than material. The graphite-versus-binder split is experimental, and the sampling intervals overlap several batch ranges; overlap is not batch equivalence.
